- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.30) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- When model shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, expect mean reversion; adjust downward by 1–2% in next 3–7 days.  
- If model forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, it often overcorrects; reduce peak forecast by 2–5% and smooth transition to true trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently forecasts above 75% of true outcome, apply downward bias correction by 5–10% for next 5–10 days unless sentiment strongly supports.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by positive recovery, model often lags; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend in such cases.
